meta.title: Notification System
meta.summary: One service that sends push and email for every team, respecting preferences, deduplicating retries and surviving provider outages.

functional: Internal services send push and email notifications through one API
Respect user preferences, opt-outs and quiet hours
Large marketing campaigns to millions of users
nonFunctional: Critical messages (one-time codes) arrive within ~5 s
No duplicate notifications when producers retry

nodes.label: Internal Services
nodes.description: Auth, orders, marketing … any team that needs to notify users

nodes.label: Notification API
nodes.description: Validates, deduplicates, applies preferences, renders templates

nodes.label: Dedupe Store
nodes.description: Idempotency keys with a 24 h TTL

nodes.label: Preferences & Devices
nodes.description: Channels, opt-outs, quiet hours, device tokens

nodes.label: Email Workers
nodes.description: Throttled to the provider's send quota

flows.title: Critical push (login code)
flows.summary: Deduplicate, check preferences, then a dedicated high-priority queue so nothing waits behind marketing.

steps.label: SET NX idem:… EX 86400
steps.detail: Producers retry on timeouts. The first call wins; a repeat with the same key is acknowledged but not sent again.

steps.label: push on, 2 devices
steps.detail: Quiet hours apply to most messages, but security codes bypass them.

steps.label: enqueue
steps.detail: Critical and bulk traffic use separate queues and workers, so a 5M-user campaign cannot delay a login code.

steps.label: 200 / 410 Unregistered
steps.detail: 410 means the app was uninstalled; the stale device token is removed so it is not retried forever.

flows.title: Marketing email campaign
flows.summary: Filter by opt-in, spread sends under the provider's quota, retry with backoff, and park permanent failures in a dead-letter queue.

steps.label: 1.4M eligible
steps.detail: Users who opted out of marketing are dropped here, which is also a legal requirement in many regions.

steps.label: token bucket 2k/s
steps.detail: Workers pace sends to the provider's quota instead of hammering it and getting throttled.

steps.label: 429 throttled (some)
steps.detail: Temporary failures are retried; permanent ones (invalid address) are not.

steps.label: retry with backoff + jitter
steps.detail: Delays grow 1 s, 4 s, 16 s … with randomness so retries do not arrive in a synchronized wave.

steps.label: after 5 attempts → DLQ
steps.detail: Nothing is silently dropped. An alert fires, and messages are replayed from the DLQ once the cause is fixed.

notes.text: Separate queues per priority (and often per channel) isolate failures: an email provider outage backs up email only, while push keeps flowing.
Delivery is at-least-once end to end. Idempotency keys at the API and message ids at the workers turn that into effectively-once for users.
Keep a second provider configured. Workers switch over when the primary's error rate crosses a threshold.
Also enforce per-user frequency caps (for example, at most 3 marketing pushes a day) so many teams cannot collectively spam a user.
Track every message's state (queued, sent, delivered, opened) in an event log for debugging and campaign analytics.
